messages:
incident-bot: PAGE | severity=P2 | Route latency p95 crossed 2500ms for /v1/generate (region=us-east-1). Paging #eng-oncall and #eng-sre
oncall-bot: Noted. Root message ts=1745312345
alice.ramirez: joining — status?
ben_eng_oncall: I'm on. Dashboards show repeated p95 spikes starting ~2024-09-16T14:14Z. It cycles approx every 60-120s
cory_sre: infra telemetry: proxy nodes show CPU/queue spikes coincident with each reroute event. Looks like a control loop causing load-induced latency
dina-routing: pulling policy state now. We have SLO-driven fallback enabled with model_variant + region fallbacks. Candidate variant redwood-7b-quant-v2 is being selected sometimes
alice.ramirez: paste the active policy blob (sanitized)
```
policy: slo-latency-primary
eval_interval_ms: 5000
p95_threshold_ms: 2500
hysteresis_ms: 15000
fallbacks:
  - kind: model_variant
    candidates: [redwood-7b, redwood-7b-quant, redwood-7b-quant-v2]
    cooldown_ms: 30000
    weigh_by: latency
  - kind: region
    candidates: [us-east-1, us-west-2]
    cooldown_ms: 20000
```
ben_eng_oncall: looks sane on paper. But controller logs show frequent swap cycles. Can you tail the controller?
dina-routing: controller tail:
```
2024-09-16T14:15:12Z policy-controller INFO eval id=slo-latency-primary p95=2630
2024-09-16T14:15:12Z policy-controller INFO fallback->model_variant target=redwood-7b-quant-v2 reason="p95>threshold"
2024-09-16T14:15:13Z route-manager INFO apply variant-swap
2024-09-16T14:15:13Z policy-controller INFO startCooldown until=2024-09-16T14:15:43
2024-09-16T14:15:44Z policy-controller INFO eval p95=2450
2024-09-16T14:15:44Z policy-controller INFO clearCooldown\n2024-09-16T14:15:44Z policy-controller INFO fallback->model_variant target=redwood-7b-quant reason="p95>threshold"
```
cory_sre: aha — cooldown gets scheduled but then cleared too quickly. The controller appears to treat single-sample p95 dips as sustained under-threshold and clears cooldown early
ben_eng_oncall: that would let the policy oscillate if p95 noise crosses threshold often. Why is cooldown cleared on a single sample?
dina-routing: our aggregator was updated recently to emit instantaneous p95 samples instead of a rolling-window aggregate due to a perf refactor. Bug introduced there.
alice.ramirez: impact calc? How much traffic touched swapped routes during the episode?
cory_sre: quick metrics run (approx): total requests in window 14:14-14:20 UTC in us-east-1 = 3,220,433. Observed p95-breaching bursts affected roughly 10-13% of traffic during swap moments (~330k-420k requests). No spike in 5xx in the window.
evan-support: Customer reports: tenants ecom-play and chat-saas filed SLO alerts and support tickets. Logged: INC-TCK-4721, INC-TCK-4722. Notifying impacted customers now
ben_eng_oncall: immediate mitigations: 1) stop auto-variant fallbacks for us-east-1 2) increase controller hysteresis/cooldowns 3) monitor for recurrence
dina-routing: I can flip the region-scoped flag to disable model_variant auto-fallback.
alice.ramirez: run the admin toggle (post output here)
```
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://admin.internal/flags --data '{"flag":"variant_auto_fallback","region":"us-east-1","value":false}'
```
ben_eng_oncall: executed. API returned 200 OK. flag.variant_auto_fallback(us-east-1)=false
cory_sre: also patching the configmap to raise cooldown/hysteresis defaults while we triage:
```
kubectl -n routing patch configmap policy-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"cooldown_ms":"120000","hysteresis_ms":"60000"}}'
```
patch applied to controller config
alice.ramirez: within ~45s of the flag flip we're seeing p95 drop back below threshold (now ~1600-1900ms). Looks stable for the moment :thumbsup:
evan-support: sending interim customer comms: "We detected transient tail-latency oscillations in US-East and have disabled automatic variant fallbacks while we patch the policy controller. We expect no further customer impact."
incident-bot: Incident state -> MITIGATED. Paging silenced for 30m
ben_eng_oncall: triage summary: root cause is twofold: 1) policy-controller aggregator change emits instantaneous p95 samples causing cooldowns to clear prematurely 2) a recently onboarded quant-v2 variant with heavier tail latency was included in weighted candidates, increasing instability when swapped
dina-routing: I opened PR to fix aggregator to use a rolling aggregate (60s window) and require two consecutive windows of breach for triggering, and symmetric logic for clearing. PR: https://git.redwood/infra/policy-controller/pull/622
cory_sre: I'll run canary rollout of the new config and aggregator in two us-east-1 controller replicas for 15m before wider rollout
alice.ramirez: follow-ups: - keep variant_auto_fallback disabled for us-east-1 until fix lands - bake raised cooldown/hysteresis into default config - add per-route circuit-breaker to limit swap rate to <=1 swap / 2 minutes - run tail-latency benchmarks on quant-v2 variants before declaring them eligible for auto-fallback\enext-steps: assign owners and file postmortem
ben_eng_oncall: creating postmortem ticket INF-9803 and assigning action items. I'll handoff follow-up to @alice.ramirez — I'm off in 40m
alice.ramirez: taking lead. I'll assemble timeline, customer-impact table, and remediation checklist. ETA: EOD for preliminary postmortem doc in #postmortems
evan-support: sent update to affected tenants and created support follow-ups
dina-routing: follow-up actions assigned to me: aggregator fix PR, add unit tests around sampling logic, ensure e2e test for cooldown semantics
cory_sre: follow-up actions assigned to me: bake config changes into helm chart, run canary rollout and monitor for 2 hours, prepare rollback plan
ben_eng_oncall: final note: if this or similar oscillation reoccurs, escalate to evergreen pager and we will run emergency rollback of routing-controller config. Thanks for the quick response everyone
alice.ramirez: logging archived traces, config snapshots, and command audit to incident archive. Will post RCA once verified
incident-bot: Incident closed -> Mitigated recorded. Please file formal postmortem with template: /incident new
-- end of thread --
